date_note: Date shown on Push Security's post; its blog index lists 23 November. The page gives no earlier day.
title: Push Security: 'GoodGuys' phishing kit sends fake paid expert-interview invitations in the names of Accenture, Nvidia, SpaceX and others
summary: Push Security says it is tracking a phishing kit it named GoodGuys that sends paid expert-interview and webinar invitations in the names of eight brands, including Accenture, Coca-Cola, Google Cloud, Nvidia and SpaceX. It says the pages collect Google work-account credentials and an operator relays codes. The researchers suspect an AI coding assistant helped build it, which they present as a suspicion.
plain: Push Security says fake interview and webinar invitations, sent in the names of well-known brands, lead to pages that steal Google work-account logins.
exec: Push Security says the pages collect Google work-account credentials, and operators relay sign-in codes.
action: General advice: treat unexpected interview or webinar invitations with caution and verify them independently; Push Security says its indicators are most useful for hunting in logs because operators rotate hosts every few days.

validation.note: Push Security's own research post read; ifeng.com (27 November, a repost of IT Home) restates it.

review.note: tag stronger than source: removed ai-enabled (Push says AI assistant use is only a suspicion); date, brands, credentials, advice match Push post
